v2_result.note: v2 stands as a failed run, next to v1. Funded companies scored 0.7 to 4.3 and none reached a take-call.

v3_changes.why: Rescoring the same ten live applications moved totals by up to 2.7 points and flipped suggestions. The cause was the scoring method, not the data: a point was taken off for every missing item the model chose to list, so a wordier answer scored lower. The low v1 and v2 backtest totals had the same cause.
scoring_fixes: Penalty for missing information is now by severity (none 0, some 1, key 2 points), not one point per listed item. Missing information still always lowers a score.
The model is told to score the evidence that exists and NOT to lower the score for what is missing. Before, it was told both, so missing data was punished twice.
Every criterion has low, middle and high behaviour anchors (no company names), so a 6 means the same thing from run to run.
Candour cannot be seen in a deck. It is a fixed neutral 5, not marked down, and flagged as needing the call, instead of a guessed score plus a penalty.
Scoring and the overlap check run at temperature 0, so the same input gives the same answer.
Numeric fluency (do they know their numbers) and unit economics (what the numbers say) are separated in the criterion wording, to stop one fact counting twice.
unchanged_on_purpose: Recommendation thresholds (take a call at 6.0 total and 5.0 in both groups; pass at 4.0 or below).
The overlap check stays over-sensitive. Overlap never changes a score; it only holds.
A hold still counts as a disagreement in the backtest.
v3_changes.known_limit: Web search is still unavailable on the free key and memo inputs are one or two paragraphs. Reported either way, with v1 and v2 beside it.

v1_result.note: v1 stands as a failed run. It is kept and reported next to v2; it is not replaced.

bug_fixes: A company was flagged as overlapping with itself when the portfolio listed it under a second name (ePlane vs The ePlane Company). Names are now matched ignoring 'company', 'technologies', 'labs' and similar endings, and a backtest never compares a company with itself.

A backtest compared each memo company with the other memo companies and with today's portfolio. The order in which the fund backed them is unknown, so the other 11 memo companies are now left out of each overlap check.

When web search was unavailable (quota), four scored criteria were each marked down for 'research failed'. An outage of our own tool is not a fact about the company, so it is now one separate note and no criterion is marked down for it.
unchanged_on_purpose: The overlap check stays over-sensitive (false alarms preferred to misses).
Missing data still lowers scores, at the same rate.
A hold still counts as a disagreement.
v2_changes.wording_only_changes_2026-11-24: src/config/rubric.ts: the candour gap text was shortened and a 'commerce_infrastructure' sector keyword list was added (the retail keyword moved out of consumer_tech). Neither changes any score or threshold, and the memos carry explicit sectors, so the v2 result is unaffected. Re-registered so the lock matches the file.
v2_changes.known_limit: Web search is still unavailable on the free key, and memo inputs are one or two paragraphs. Scores will still rest on very little information, so v2 may still fail. Reported either way.

purpose: Pass/fail criteria for trusting the triage system, fixed BEFORE the first backtest run. Changing this file after registration makes the backtest refuse to run until re-registered (and the re-registration is logged).
unit_of_agreement: System recommendation compared with the fund's real decision: take_call <-> invested, pass <-> passed. A 'hold' is counted as a disagreement for the agreement rate (the system declined to make the case) and is reported separately.
criterion_hit_definition: For each labelled criterion on each memo (data/backtest/memos.json 'expected'): 'high' hits when score >= 6, 'low' hits when score <= 5, 'mid' hits when 4 <= score <= 7.
verdict_rule: TRUST (for advisory use only) if every threshold is met. Otherwise NOT YET: the failing metric names what to fix. Missing data and the candour criterion are excluded from nothing: they are scored as designed.
labelling_rule: Each disagreement gets a one-paragraph judgement citing the memo's reason text. Labelling happens AFTER the run, by a human, and is not used to tune thresholds.
caveats_to_state: n=12 is small: one flip moves agreement by 8 points.
Memo inputs are richer than real applications; the 'what it does' text was written by the fund after meeting the company.
Rubric v0 was drafted from these same memos, so the backtest is in-sample for the rubric. Scoring prompts withhold the memo-derived seed_evidence to limit this.
Research cut-off dates are assumptions (decision dates are not in the pack) and web search cannot be fully date-blocked; outcome-like snippets are flagged and excluded.
Prepnest, and the other uneasy passes, are the interesting disagreements; the fund itself is unsure about them.
